rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for an unwanted delay holding up a scheduled event, service, or activity.

example.english: The flight had a delay because of heavy rain.
example.jyutping: baan1 gei1 jan1 wai6 daai6 jyu5 jau5 jin4 ng6

rows.note: Use this for a neutral postponement or time lag, especially with sounds, signals, technology, or deliberately putting something off.

example.english: This audio recording has a slight delay.
example.jyutping: ni1 dyun6 luk6 jam1 jau5 siu2 siu2 jin4 ci4

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken verb when someone or something holds up, stops, or hinders progress.

example.english: Traffic caused a delay on my way to work.
example.jyutping: sak1 ce1 zo2 zyu6 ngo5 faan1 gung1

rows.note: Use this when something retards progress or makes a process move more slowly rather than stopping it outright.

example.english: Too much paperwork caused a delay in the approval process.
example.traditional: 太多文件拖慢咗個審批程序。
example.jyutping: taai3 do1 man4 gin6 to1 maan6 zo2 go3 sam2 pai1 cing4 zeoi6

rows.note: Use this for postponing a scheduled event, appointment, deadline, or arrangement to a later time.

example.english: They decided to delay the meeting until next week.
example.traditional: 佢哋決定將個會議押後到下星期。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 kyut3 ding6 zoeng1 go3 wui6 ji5 aat3 hau6 dou3 haa6 sing1 kei4

rows.note: Use this very natural spoken construction when putting off doing an action until later.

example.english: I’ll delay replying to you until later.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ci4 di1 sin1 fuk1 nei5
